content.text:
I migrated all four modules in `src/services/` (`user-service`, `order-service`, `payment-service`, `auth-service`) to the repository pattern, and each one's tests pass (2 passing, 0 failing). Two of them leave the API broken, though.

**Broken callers:** `src/api/routes.js` was outside the migration scope, so it still passes callbacks to functions that now return promises:
- line 8: `listActiveUsers(cb)`
- line 9: `findUser(id, cb)`
- line 12: `uncapturedTotalCents(cb)`

Those three routes (`/users`, `/users/:id` and `/reports/uncaptured-total`) won't work until `routes.js` is updated to use the promise-returning versions. Don't ship the user-service and payment-service changes before that.

**Other things to know before merging:**
- The migration also edited all four test files in `tests/`. Some test edits are expected when function signatures change, but review those diffs to make sure the passing tests still check the same behaviour.
- It created one new file, `src/repositories/payment-repository.js`. The other three modules presumably use repository classes that already existed, but the reports don't say which.
- It left a scratch directory, `.agent-work/`, which is untracked. Delete it or add it to `.gitignore`.

Nothing is committed. If you want, I can update `routes.js` to the promise-based calls and then run the full test suite.
